implementation_notes: Structured concurrency is a first-class design goal of Swift's concurrency model: withTaskGroup/withThrowingTaskGroup create a scope that always waits for all of its child tasks before returning (Apple's documentation states this even holds for cancelled tasks) and is empty afterwards, a throwing child cancels the group and its error surfaces at the group's await point, and async let children are implicitly awaited at the end of the enclosing scope. Cancellation is cooperative through Task.isCancelled and try Task.checkCancellation().
pitfalls: Children must check cancellation; a task that never polls Task.isCancelled makes the group wait until it finishes naturally.
A non-throwing withTaskGroup does not cancel siblings when one child fails - collect per-child errors explicitly or use the throwing variant.
Task.detached escapes the scope (no parent-child lifetime link) and should be used only for work that is intentionally owned elsewhere.
